headline: California's athletic commission told robot-fighting startup REK to stop holding unsanctioned human-versus-robot cage fights after YouTuber Frankie LaPenna fought three of its humanoid robots.
score_reason: Pool score 4 kept as the late gap-fill instruction says: a viral robot stunt with a small legal angle; the fight (18 Sep 2026) and the letter (30 Sep 2026) are before the window, so the usual stale rule would lower it by 1.
importance_line: The commission treats fights between people and robots like any other combat-sport contest, which affects fighters and organisers first, but it is unclear whether REK will stage another bout with a human or whether robot-only fights are covered, and reports differ on how the fight went.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports, quoting a cease-and-desist letter that REK chief executive Cix Liv posted on X on 30 Sep 2026 with the words "We made it boys", that California's state athletic commission, which oversees combat sports, ordered the robot-fighting startup to stop holding or promoting boxing or martial-arts contests involving a human without its approval, and warned that holding one without a licence is a misdemeanour. The letter refers to an 18 Sep 2026 bout in San Francisco in which YouTuber Frankie LaPenna fought three REK humanoid robots, which Fox News, citing REK's technology partner Reflex Arc, says were steered by human pilots.
